item.text: The implementation chooses the conventional numeric median for even-length arrays: sort the values and average the two middle values. I’m recording that explicitly now so the tradeoff is visible in the job history.

arguments.context: The new median helper needed a defined behavior for even-length numeric lists, where there is no single middle element.
arguments.choice: For even-length lists, median returns the arithmetic mean of the two middle values after numeric sorting.
arguments.rationale: The existing helpers are numeric statistical helpers, and averaging the two central sorted values is the standard numeric median definition. It also preserves fractional medians such as [1, 2, 3, 4] -> 2.5 instead of biasing lower or higher.

alternatives.rejectedBecause: This would bias the result downward and is less conventional for a general numeric statistics helper.
This would bias the result upward and is less conventional for a general numeric statistics helper.
